# Lisbon Family Trip Plan: 10–15 Apr 2026

A 5-day Lisbon stay for 2 adults + 2 children can fit your **€2,800** budget comfortably if you mix free parks, a few paid attractions, and use transit instead of taxis. I’m assuming you want a centrally located apartment or family room, moderate meals, and one easy beach day by train.

## Day-by-Day Lisbon Itinerary

### Day 1: Baixa, Chiado, and the Riverfront
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and do a gentle walk through **Baixa** and **Rossio**.
- Afternoon: Ride the **Santa Justa area** only if energy is high; otherwise keep it easy with **Rua Augusta** and the **riverfront promenade**.
- Dinner: Family-friendly Portuguese meal in **Chiado** or **Cais do Sodré**.
- Estimated cost: **€180–€260** for meals, transit, and light activities.

### Day 2: Kid-Friendly Museums and Parque das Nações
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: **Pavilhão do Conhecimento** (science museum) in Parque das Nações.
- Afternoon: Walk the waterfront, playgrounds, and indoor/outdoor spaces near the **Oceanário** area; choose the aquarium only if your kids love marine life.
- Dinner: Casual meal in **Parque das Nações** with easy metro access.
- Estimated cost: **€220–€360** depending on museum tickets and whether you add the aquarium.

### Day 3: Alfama, Tram 28 Area, and Castelo Views
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- Morning: Explore **Alfama** early before crowds; keep it stroller-light and use short walking loops.
- Afternoon: Visit **Castelo de São Jorge** or replace it with a slower viewpoint-and-snack day if the children prefer less climbing.
- Dinner: Early dinner back in **Baixa/Chiado** for a simple transit return.
- Estimated cost: **€160–€280** for admissions, snacks, and transit.

### Day 4: Beach Day in Cascais
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: Take the train from **Cais do Sodré to Cascais** for an easy day trip.
- Afternoon: Beach time at **Praia da Rainha** or a calmer stretch near the promenade; add a seaside walk and ice cream stop.
- Dinner: Seafood or casual pizza in **Cascais**, then train back to Lisbon.
- Estimated cost: **€180–€320** including train, beach extras, and dinner.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3c/Beach_near_Lisbon_Portugal%2C_1994..jpg Alt=Estimated cost: **€180–€320** including train, beach extras, and dinner, Lisbon, Portugal

### Day 5: Jardim da Estrela, Tram/Metro Easy Day, and Souvenirs
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Relax in **Jardim da Estrela** or **Parque Eduardo VII**.
- Afternoon: Last shopping and café time in **Avenida da Liberdade** or **Príncipe Real**.
- Dinner: Finish with a family dinner near your hotel for an easy departure next day.
- Estimated cost: **€150–€240**.

## Family Budget Breakdown and Stay Areas

| Item | Best Fit | Est. Cost |
|---|---|---:|
| Accommodation | 2-bedroom apartment or family room in central Lisbon | €1,050–€1,500 |
| Food | Mix of cafés, casual lunches, and simple dinners | €650–€900 |
| Transit | Metro, tram, train to Cascais, occasional taxi | €90–€180 |
| Attractions | 2–4 paid entries total | €250–€500 |
| Snacks/ice cream/incidentals | Buffer for kids’ extras | €120–€220 |
| Total | Target range | **€2,160–€3,300** |

### Best neighborhoods to stay in
- **Baixa/Chiado**: Best overall for first-time visitors, walkable, great transit, easy for families.
- **Avenida da Liberdade**: Quieter, more spacious hotels, excellent metro access.
- **Parque das Nações**: Best for modern apartments, waterfront space, and easy airport access.
- **Príncipe Real**: Nice cafés and parks, but some streets are hillier.
- **Avoid if you want easiest family logistics**: steep upper **Alfama** streets for a base, unless you’re comfortable with lots of walking.

## Reservations to Book Ahead

- **Accommodation**: book early for a family-sized place in Baixa, Chiado, or Avenida da Liberdade.
- **Pavilhão do Conhecimento**: reserve timed entry if available, especially for a weekend or school holiday period.
- **Oceanário de Lisboa**: book ahead if you plan to include it; it is one of the most popular family attractions.
- **Castelo de São Jorge**: prebook if you want to avoid queues.
- **Cascais train day**: no reservation usually needed, but plan timing for a smooth beach day.
- **Airport transfer or family taxi**: useful if arriving late or with luggage and tired kids.
